name: Using AI well
strandNote: Optional for every quant role. For machine learning research roles, and for using and building AI tools with judgement.
description: Learn how a chatbot is made and why it makes things up, then ask it well, check what it says and know the risks.

requires.why: Pretraining is next-word prediction at scale, which ai-basics level 4 builds by counting.

lessonObjectives.l1-reading-the-internet: Describe pretraining as learning to predict the next token of a huge body of text.
lessonObjectives.l2-from-predictor-to-assistant: Explain how fine-tuning on example conversations turns a text predictor into an assistant.
lessonObjectives.l3-learning-from-preferences: Describe how people's rankings of answers shape a chatbot's replies.
lessonObjectives.l4-confident-and-wrong: Explain why a model that predicts likely text can state false facts fluently.
lessonObjectives.l5-asking-well: Write a request that gives the task, the context, the format and an example.
lessonObjectives.l6-checking-the-sums: Check an AI answer's arithmetic with an estimate, and recompute it when it matters.
lessonObjectives.l7-checking-claims: Tell a checkable claim from an uncheckable one, and check that a quoted source says what is claimed.
lessonObjectives.l8-asking-for-the-working: Ask for step-by-step working, check each step, and tell when a chatbot is the wrong tool for the job.
lessonObjectives.l9-what-not-to-paste: Decide what is safe to paste into a chatbot, and remove the details that identify people or firms.
lessonObjectives.l10-bias-from-data: Spot bias in a chatbot's answers that comes from the examples it learned from.
lessonObjectives.l11-misuse-and-fakes: Recognise common misuses of AI: cheating on assessed work, fake reviews, scams and faked media.
lessonObjectives.l12-what-alignment-means: Describe in plain words what it means for an AI system to do what its makers intend, and why that is hard.
